headline: Highest risk is data leakage and cascading error from ms-swift’s file/API handling into a non-isolated game-playing agent, while prompt-injection risk is limited by the lack of a shared channel.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared communication channel is documented between godot_rl_agents and ms-swift. agent_a has no filesystem, clipboard, or MCP surfaces, while agent_b’s documented stdin/stdout and files are not bridged to agent_a. Without a bridge, prompt injection is not plausible.
conditions: IF a shared filesystem, clipboard, or message queue is added between the agents, reassess injection risk.
IF agent_a begins parsing agent_b output as instructions, the risk becomes non-none.
mitigations: Keep the agents disconnected except for explicit, typed APIs.
Do not pipe raw agent_b text into agent_a prompts.
Add provenance tags to any exchanged artifacts.
requires-engineering: introduce a sanitizer for any future shared channel.

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_b can read and write files and call external APIs, and it handles hub/sdk tokens plus many data classes. agent_a is docs-only and shows no data surfaces, but if the pair shares a workspace, agent_b could ingest and transmit local artifacts. The interaction is plausible in default CLI workflows, so uncertainty stays medium.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same directory, agent_b can access artifacts created for agent_a.
IF agent_b is given files containing secrets or sensitive datasets, those contents may flow to external APIs.
mitigations: Use separate working directories for each agent.
Store secrets outside any shared path.
Disable network egress for agent_b during local runs.
Review file globs before launching agent_b.
requires-engineering: add workspace isolation or mount namespaces.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: agent_a has no write or network capabilities, so it cannot contend for mutable resources. agent_b can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses, but modify_git_state is false and no shared mutable target is documented. The only plausible conflict is if an operator manually points both at the same files.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to write the same directory, file clobbering becomes possible.
IF a shared git repo is introduced and agent_b is extended to modify git state, conflict risk increases.
mitigations: Assign distinct output directories.
Run one agent at a time on shared artifacts.
Use read-only mounts for agent_a inputs.
Check for existing files before agent_b writes.
requires-engineering: add locking for any future shared mutable store.

D_cascading_error.rationale: agent_b’s CLI/Python workflow can consume files and outputs, so if it treats agent_a-generated artifacts as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream actions. agent_a is a game-playing package with no documented verification or safety layer, so its outputs should not be assumed reliable. The pathway exists, but no direct action authority is documented.
conditions: IF agent_b ingests agent_a outputs without validation, incorrect facts can propagate.
IF agent_b is configured to auto-run evaluations or training steps from those outputs, the blast radius expands.
mitigations: Require human review before acting on agent_a outputs.
Validate schemas for any exchanged files.
Keep agent_a outputs as advisory only.
Log and diff all downstream actions.
requires-engineering: add verification gates before execution.

E_compliance.rationale: agent_b explicitly handles hub/sdk tokens and multiple data classes, while agent_a is open-source docs-only with no data surfaces. If regulated data is processed through ms-swift, its networked API calls and file handling can create residency or retention mismatches. The pair itself is not enough to prove a violation, so medium is the cautious choice.
conditions: IF regulated data is routed through agent_b to external APIs, residency or retention obligations may be triggered.
IF the operator requires local-only processing, agent_b’s allowlisted egress must be constrained.
mitigations: Confirm data-class handling before use.
Avoid sending regulated data to agent_b.
Restrict agent_b egress to approved endpoints only.
Set short retention for logs and outputs.
requires-engineering: enforce policy-based routing and retention controls.
